title: BMA agent executor types
description: Agent executor capability: the platform sends natural-language turns to an executor that runs a complete agent (model loop and tools) locally, and the executor streams Anthropic Managed Agents events back. See docs/architecture/executor-agent-capability.zh-CN.md.

AgentCapability.description: agent capability. Present with enabled=true when the executor runs a complete agent and accepts turn.start, turn.input, turn.cancel, session.close and interaction.response (and agent.custom_tool_result when custom_tools is true).

models.description: Models the local agent can run. An empty list means the executor picks its own model and ignores AgentTurnConfig.model.

permission_modes.description: Permission mode ids the local agent understands, for example default, accept_edits, plan, bypass_permissions. The executor defines the ids; the platform only passes one back in AgentTurnConfig.permission_mode.

interaction_kinds.description: Interaction kinds the executor may open with interaction.request.

file_inputs.description: The executor fetches the bytes of the file blocks (file_id) of turn.start and turn.input itself. Declare it only when it can: through the tools endpoint of the turn (tools_mcp_url and tools_mcp_token in turn.start metadata, GET <tools_mcp_url without /mcp>/files/<file_id>/content), or, on a machine daemon token, through the turn input files routes (GET /v1/machines/{machine_id}/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id}/input_files and .../{file_id}/content, docs/architecture/executor-turn-input-files.md). Together with the agent accepting images (harness.image_inputs) it is what lets the platform accept an image input for the agent: without it the input is refused with 400, with it the platform sends the file blocks and never refuses an image the agent accepts. Absent means false.

max_sessions.description: Turns the executor runs at once. A turn.start while that many turns are running answers -32009 executor_busy (retryable). A session with no running turn holds no slot; an executor may release the local resources of its least recently used idle sessions and load them again from executor_session_ref on the next turn.start.

turn_resume.description: The executor keeps the state of its turns across a process restart. When it registers again without a session whose turn was running, the platform starts the same turn again in a new event epoch (turn.start with the same turn_id, input_id and executor_session_ref, then the turn.input the turn already received) and the executor continues the turn from its own state. Without it such a turn ends failed (session.error, session.status_idle retries_exhausted) and is not sent again: an executor without that state would run the turn again from its opening input and repeat tool calls whose effects already happened.

platform_credentials.description: Per-turn credentials the executor asks the platform to hand it in turn.start metadata: brain_tools (tools_mcp_url, tools_mcp_token: the session's tools endpoint) and harness_model (model_base_url, model_token: the session's model endpoint; optionally model_context_window and model_max_output_tokens, positive integer strings: the resolved model's context window and output ceiling, absent when the platform has no catalog entry for the model, in which case the executor uses its own defaults). A declaration only states what the executor can use; the platform decides by the executor's identity: a platform service executor gets what it declares; on a platform-managed pool machine an ACP harness turn gets harness_model by default, without a declaration; a BYO machine gets harness_model only when it declares it, and an undeclared BYO machine gets nothing, so it keeps using the model endpoint configured on it and the platform never overrides that upstream. brain_tools (contract 1.4.0) is handed to a tenant executor only when the session binds this machine as the brain machine and a different machine as the hands machine (brain and hands apart, ADR-0029) and the executor declared brain_tools; the token is bound to the org, the session, the turn, this machine and the brain epoch of the turn (the event epoch of the turn.start that carries it), so a turn started again in a new epoch gets a new token and calls made with the previous epoch's token are refused. When one machine is both brain and hands nothing is handed (the executor runs its tools itself); a platform service executor and an executor that did not declare brain_tools never get it. Until contract 1.4.0 brain_tools was never handed to a tenant executor. The harness_model token is a bma-model token bound to the turn's org, session, turn and machine (model_base_url is the machine's proxy path). Tokens are computed for each turn.start, are valid until the turn ends, and are never stored.

custom_tools.description: The executor runs custom tools defined by the platform agent: it emits agent.custom_tool_use for a call to one and waits for agent.custom_tool_result. Without it the platform never sends agent.custom_tool_result and answers a user.custom_tool_result for the session with an error.

harness.description: Deprecated: one hosted agent. Use harnesses; an executor that sets both lists this one in harnesses too.

harnesses.description: Every third-party agent the executor can host, by distinct id (for example dsh and claude-code). The platform picks one per turn with AgentTurnConfig.harness; an executor declares only agents that are installed and passed their self-check.

input_skills.description: Accepts exact, input-bound selected skill documents and reports their installed versions in TurnStartResult.effective.input_skill_receipt. Absent or false: do not send selected skills.

context_maintenance.description: Explicit idle session.compact and session.compact_cancel with durable versioned receipts. Absent means unsupported. The executor reserves the session independently of ordinary turns, preserves original history, and publishes replacement context only after durable success. It must not declare this before the complete maintenance contract is implemented.

AgentHarnessCapability.description: What the third-party agent the executor hosts (for example an ACP agent) supports; an omitted boolean is false. Sent with executor.capabilities.update once the agent has started; absent until then and after a reconnect until the next turn. Informational: the platform records it and reflects it in the session harness capabilities.

id.description: Agent profile id, for example dsh.

protocol.description: Protocol the executor speaks to the agent, for example acp/1.

agent_name.description: Name the agent reported about itself (ACP initialize agentInfo.name).

agent_version.description: Version the agent reported about itself (ACP initialize agentInfo.version); may differ from version.

streaming.description: token: agent.message and agent.thinking stream as deltas. committed: each message arrives whole once the agent committed it.

session_resume.description: A conversation continues in a new agent process (ACP session/resume).

session_load.description: A conversation can be reloaded with its history replayed (ACP session/load).

permission_relay.description: Which tool calls reach interaction.request. full: every call the agent's policy asks about. escalation_only: only calls that leave the agent's own sandbox; calls inside it (including workspace writes) are never asked. none: the agent never asks, so platform approval covers no tool call.

structured_errors.description: The agent reports typed errors; false means session.error carries agent_error with the agent's text.

usage.description: tokens: the agent reports token usage. context_only: it reports context window occupancy only; usage is metered by the model proxy.

AgentModel.description: One model the local agent can run.

thinking_levels.description: Thinking or reasoning-effort levels the model accepts, lowest first. Use the reasoning effort values of the model APIs: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (OpenAI reasoning_effort; Claude Code effort levels are low, medium, high, xhigh, max). An executor that drives an OpenAI-compatible endpoint sends the level as reasoning_effort unchanged. Empty or absent: the model takes no level and AgentTurnConfig.thinking_level is not applied.

default_thinking_level.description: Level applied when the turn names none; one of thinking_levels. Absent: no level is sent and the model uses its own default.

AgentTurnConfig.description: Requested (turn.start) or effective (TurnStartResult.effective) turn configuration. Every member is optional in a request; the executor reports the values it actually applied.

model.description: Model the turn runs on. When the capability lists models it must be one of models[].id: an executor answers any other with -32602 invalid params and never substitutes another model. When the capability lists no models the executor picks its own model and ignores this member; effective then reports the model it used.

thinking_level.description: Reasoning effort of the turn: one of the thinking_levels of the turn's model (AgentModel). Absent: the model's default_thinking_level, or none. A level the model does not list answers -32602 invalid params; for a model that lists no levels the member is ignored and effective omits it.

permission_mode.description: One of the capability permission_modes. Absent: the executor's default mode. turn.start metadata tool_policy, when present, refines the permission of single tools on top of the mode.

cwd.description: Working directory on the executor host. The executor rejects a directory outside its allowed roots with -32001 forbidden. When turn.start metadata carries tools_mcp_* (brain and hands on different machines, contract 1.4.0) cwd is a path on the hands machine: the executor does not check it against its own allowed roots and does not create a workspace for it on this machine; the hands machine's own policy applies when a tool runs there.

environment_info.description: Contract 1.4.0, optional. Sent only when brain and hands are on different machines (turn.start metadata carries tools_mcp_*): describes the hands machine, so the brain can tell the model where its tools run. Omitted when brain and hands are the same machine, and absent from TurnStartResult.effective.

system.description: Extra system instructions from the platform agent definition.

harness.description: Id of the hosted agent (one of the capability harnesses[].id) the turn runs on. Omitted: the executor's only harness. An id the executor does not host answers -32012 capability_unavailable.

input_skills.description: Requested only. Exact authorized skill revisions for this opening input; never mutates session defaults. Requires agent.input_skills. The platform revalidates grants and the session frozen subset before dispatch.

input_skill_receipt.description: Effective only. Returned after exact selected skill bytes have been installed for the opening input. Missing or mismatched receipt is not successful skill preparation.

AgentInputBlock.description: One block of user input. A file block references a platform session file by file_id; the executor downloads it through the executor files API. File bytes never travel on the control channel.

TurnStartResult.description: turn.start result. Idempotent by turn_id: a repeated turn.start for a turn the executor already accepted returns the same result without starting a second run.

executor_session_ref.description: Opaque local session handle (for example the local agent's conversation id). The platform stores it and sends it back in the next turn.start so the executor can resume the local conversation after a restart.

resumed.description: true when the executor continued an existing local conversation, false when it started a new one.

TurnCancelResult.description: turn.cancel result. canceled=false when the turn is unknown or already ended; the turn still ends with its own session.status_idle event.

EnvironmentInfo.description: Contract 1.4.0. The hands machine as the platform knows it (AgentTurnConfig.environment_info), from the hands executor's registration and the session's file mounts. Every member is optional; an omitted member is unknown, not empty. Values describe the machine at the time of turn.start.

os.description: Operating system of the hands machine, as ExecutorInfo.os (for example linux, darwin, windows).

shell.description: Shell the bash tool runs commands with on the hands machine (for example bash, zsh, powershell).

cwd.description: Default working directory of tools on the hands machine; the same value as AgentTurnConfig.cwd when that is set.

session_files_root.description: Directory on the hands machine where the session's files are mounted, when the hands executor declared session_files.

ToolsTokenRefreshResult.description: Contract 1.4.0. tools_token.refresh result: the credential for the turn's next platform tool calls, in the form of the turn.start metadata tools_mcp_url, tools_mcp_token and tools_mcp_token_expires_at.

tools_mcp_token.description: Bearer token for tools_mcp_url, bound to the org, session, turn, brain machine and brain epoch of the turn. Valid until expires_at.

tools_mcp_url.description: The session's platform tools endpoint the token is for (https://<executor host>/v1/machines/{brain_machine_id}/mcp).

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 time the token stops being accepted.

ModelTokenRefreshResult.description: model_token.refresh result: the credential for the turn's next model calls, in the form of the turn.start metadata model_base_url and model_token.

model_token.description: Bearer token for model_base_url. Valid until expires_at.

model_base_url.description: Base URL the token is for (an OpenAI / Anthropic base URL path).

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 time the token stops being accepted.

AgentEventType.description: Durable events an agent executor emits with session.event. Names and members follow Anthropic Managed Agents session events. user.* events are written by the platform, never by the executor.

AgentEvent.description: One durable agent event. The event id is the session.event event_id; agent.tool_result.tool_use_id references the event_id of its agent.tool_use.

AgentMessageEvent.description: Final assistant text. Streaming previews for the same event_id arrive earlier as session.event_delta.

AgentThinkingEvent.description: Model thinking. content may be empty when the model only reports that it thought.

EvaluatedPermission.description: Permission decision the executor applied to a tool use. ask means the executor opened an interaction.request for it.

AgentToolUseEvent.description: A built-in or custom tool the local agent is calling. Its event_id is the tool_use_id.

AgentCustomToolUseEvent.description: A custom tool the local agent is calling: a tool the user's application runs and answers (capability agent.custom_tools). Its event_id is the tool_use_id. The platform shows the session as waiting (session.status_idle with stop_reason requires_action naming the event) and delivers the user's result with agent.custom_tool_result. The turn stays open while the executor waits: the executor does not send session.status_idle for it. If its own timeout passes first, the executor ends the call with a failed agent.tool_result naming this event.

CustomToolResultResult.description: agent.custom_tool_result result. accepted=true: the executor took the result for the call it was waiting on. accepted=false: it no longer waits (unknown tool_use_id, already answered, timed out, or canceled with its turn); the platform marks its copy stale and does not send it again.

AgentMcpToolUseEvent.description: An MCP tool the local agent is calling. Its event_id is the mcp_tool_use_id.

SessionStatusRunningEvent.description: The local agent started working on the turn.

StopReasonType.description: Anthropic stop_reason types an executor may report. requires_action is not in the list: the platform projects it from open interactions.

TurnOutcome.description: BMA extension on session.status_idle: how the turn ended.

SessionStatusIdleEvent.description: The turn ended. It is the last event of its turn_id; the platform publishes the turn as finished only after it accepted this event and every lower sequence.

AgentErrorCode.description: Stop code table: the error types an agent executor reports for a turn that ended failed, so every agent (Go ACP harness, brain hosts, local desktop agents) says the same thing for the same cause. output_limit_reached: the model reply was cut at its output-token limit (ACP stopReason max_tokens, DSH max-tokens, finish_reason length). context_too_large: the conversation does not fit the model context window even after compaction. model_stream_idle: the model stream sent no data for the idle limit (default 90 s). agent_error: any other failure of the agent. agent_unavailable: the agent process is gone or did not answer a cancel in time. agent_auth_required: the agent needs credentials it does not have. agent_protocol_error: the agent rejected the request as malformed or unsupported. A code is the type of session.error; an executor whose SDK cannot set the type yet (structured_errors false) puts it first in the message as '<code>: <detail>', and the platform reads both forms. The platform keeps the code in error.code and projects a type outside the official session.error union to unknown_error; a platform may map a code to an official type itself (context_too_large to compaction_limit_reached_error, ADR-0010). Executors report only these values; a new cause adds a value here first.

type.description: An AgentErrorCode value; other strings are tolerated (objects accept unknown members) and projected as unknown_error.

SessionErrorEvent.description: A turn-level error. A failed turn still ends with session.status_idle turn_outcome=failed.

EventDeltaType.description: Durable event type a streaming preview belongs to.

InteractionKind.description: Interaction kinds; they map 1:1 to platform agent interactions.

InteractionScope.description: How long a permission grant lasts on the executor: this tool use only, or the rest of the session.

InteractionQuestionOption.description: One answer option of a question interaction.

InteractionRequestResult.description: interaction.request result. Idempotent by interaction_id: a repeat returns the same platform interaction. platform_interaction_id equals interaction_id when that is an appr_ plus 24 lower-case hex id (adopted); otherwise it is the platform-assigned int_ id.

InteractionOutcome.description: How the platform resolved an interaction. allow/deny answer permission, answered answers question, expired and canceled close either kind without an answer.

InteractionResponder.description: Who answered, for local audit. surface is the client that resolved it, for example desktop, mobile, web, slack.

InteractionResponseResult.description: interaction.response result. accepted=false when the interaction is unknown or already resolved (first answer wins); the platform then marks its copy stale.

InteractionCancelReason.description: Why the executor withdrew an open interaction.

InputSkillDocument.description: Exact SKILL.md bytes for one authorized frozen revision. Hash covers UTF-8 body bytes, independently verified by the executor. At most 256 KiB across the selected documents.

SessionCompactResult.description: Durable context replacement receipt. No user message or ordinary turn is created. The operation id and original version identify an immutable retry even after newer compactions.

SessionCompactCancelResult.description: A durable publication fence or the already-applied receipt. settled is filled by the SDK, independently from the handler's fence.
